alternate_names: Sri Sri Radha Damodar Mandir, Sohna Road

history.period: Congregation from c. 2002; complex donated 2015; grand temple inaugurated 26-27 November 2022
history.summary: The ISKCON Sri Sri Radha Damodar Mandir is the 'Glory of Gurugram' - ISKCON's grand temple near Badshahpur on Sohna Road (Sector 67, Sushant Lok IV). The Gurugram congregation grew over about 22 years from a small preaching centre into a full temple. The complex was donated by educationist Acharya Sudarshan Maharaj in 2015 and renovated over three years in Rajasthani palace style (design by HG Rasapriya das, funded by industrialist HG Vedavyas das), with handmade Nathdwara/Jaipuri paintings, Makrana marble floors and Jodhpur teakwood doors. The deities Sri Sri Radha Damodar and Sri Sri Gaura Nitai were installed on 26 November 2022, at a multi-day inauguration attended by Haryana Governor Bandaru Dattatreya and ISKCON GBC leaders including HH Gopal Krishna Goswami - fulfilling, per ISKCON, Srila Prabhupada's wish for temples around Hastinapur (Delhi). The centre runs Sunday feasts, Rath Yatra, Food for Life prasad distribution, value-education and kirtan programmes. It is an extension centre of ISKCON Delhi.

name: ISKCON Temple (Sri Sri Radha Damodar)
town_description: Gurugram (formerly Gurgaon) is a major satellite city of Delhi in Haryana's National Capital Region and one of India's biggest IT, finance and startup hubs - the 'Millennium City'. Its name derives from Guru Dronacharya, whose ashram is traditionally placed here. The ISKCON temple stands in the Badshahpur/Sector 67 area on Sohna Road in the city's southern expansion zone.
